g_6dbf2e0385b0.description: Add a snapshot() method to ToolPerformanceTracker in scaffold/agent/core/performance_tracker.py. snapshot() returns a dict: {total_tasks, success_rate (float 0-1), avg_latency_ms, best_model (str or None)}. Then in scaffold/agent/orchestrator.py, at the end of the EXECUTION SUMMARY print block, add a one-line print of the snapshot: '[TRACKER] total=X success=Y% avg_ms=Z best=M'

g_ab652806529c.description: Add a snapshot() method to the ToolPerformanceTracker class that computes and returns a summary dict with keys: total_tasks (int), success_rate (float 0-1), avg_latency_ms (float), best_model (str or None). Use existing internal tracking data (task records, latencies, model performance) already stored on the instance.

tasks.action: Add a snapshot() method to the ToolPerformanceTracker class that computes and returns a summary dict with keys: total_tasks (int), success_rate (float 0-1), avg_latency_ms (float), best_model (str or None). Use existing internal tracking data (task records, latencies, model performance) already stored on the instance.
tasks.interface_contract: Called on a ToolPerformanceTracker instance with no arguments; returns a plain dict with exactly four keys
constraints: Return dict must have exactly these keys: 'total_tasks', 'success_rate', 'avg_latency_ms', 'best_model'
success_rate must be a float in range [0.0, 1.0]; return 0.0 if total_tasks is 0
avg_latency_ms must be a float; return 0.0 if no latency data is available
best_model must be a str (model name with highest success count) or None if no model data exists
Must not raise exceptions when tracker has recorded zero tasks
must_not: Must not modify any instance state
Must not make network or file I/O calls
Must not import new top-level modules not already used in the file
tasks.example_call: tracker = ToolPerformanceTracker(); snap = tracker.snapshot(); assert 'total_tasks' in snap

g_37433d787cf7.description: At the end of the existing EXECUTION SUMMARY print block, call self.tracker.snapshot() (or however the tracker is accessed in the orchestrator) and print a single formatted line: '[TRACKER] total=X success=Y% avg_ms=Z best=M' where Y is success_rate*100 rounded to 1 decimal, Z is avg_latency_ms rounded to 1 decimal, M is best_model or 'None'.

tasks.action: At the end of the existing EXECUTION SUMMARY print block, call self.tracker.snapshot() (or however the tracker is accessed in the orchestrator) and print a single formatted line: '[TRACKER] total=X success=Y% avg_ms=Z best=M' where Y is success_rate*100 rounded to 1 decimal, Z is avg_latency_ms rounded to 1 decimal, M is best_model or 'None'.
tasks.function_signature: # No new function; inline addition inside the existing summary print block
tasks.interface_contract: The print statement executes immediately after the last line of the EXECUTION SUMMARY block during each orchestration run
constraints: success percent must be formatted as e.g. '72.3%' (one decimal place)
avg_ms must be formatted as e.g. '145.2' (one decimal place)
best_model must print as the string value or the literal 'None' if the value is None
Must call snapshot() on the same tracker object already used in the orchestrator; do not instantiate a new tracker
Print must be a single print() call producing exactly one output line
must_not: Must not alter any existing print statements in the summary block
Must not wrap the print in a try/except that silently swallows errors
tasks.example_call: snap = self.tracker.snapshot(); print(f'[TRACKER] total={snap["total_tasks"]} success={snap["success_rate"]*100:.1f}% avg_ms={snap["avg_latency_ms"]:.1f} best={snap["best_model"]}')
